inspection_summary: Inspected all 1171 normalized lines. The article develops a reusable chain from fractional-part discrepancy of zero ordinates to exponential sums, and from those sums in two directions to prime-counting fluctuations and pair correlation. Its proofs expose smoothing, band-limited approximation, explicit-formula transfer, and second-difference control as the main mechanisms. The final section transfers the framework to primitive Selberg-class L-functions, while isolating a genuine degree-dependent transition-zone obstruction. Formula extraction is mostly recoverable from surrounding prose; the full-page histogram extraction is not independently usable without the retained PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the problem: fractional parts of scaled zero ordinates, their lower-order distribution, and connections to short-interval primes and pair correlation.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction and statement of results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the lower-order density g_alpha and discrepancy, states the exponential-sum, short-interval-prime, and pair-correlation conjectural routes, and records their implication structure.

sections_inspected.label: Proofs of Theorems 1-4
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Implements sharp-to-smooth transfer with mollification and extremal trigonometric polynomials, connects zero sums to local prime fluctuations by a band-limited cutoff and explicit formula, and converts pair-correlation regularity into exponential-sum cancellation.

sections_inspected.label: General L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the Selberg-class setting, generalized bias and discrepancy, transfers the zero-sum/prime-sum mechanisms, and diagnoses the pair-correlation transition-zone obstruction for degree at least two.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgement and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-substantive closing matter and bibliography, inspected for completeness but not selected as semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic resonance produces the lower-order density
accepted_units.why_material: Separates uniform distribution from its first systematic lower-order correction: g_alpha vanishes except when alpha is a rational multiple of log p/(2 pi), where an Euler-prime resonance creates a periodic bias. Conjecture 1 sharpens the smooth-test-function result to interval indicators.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the zero-count normalization, the definition of g_alpha, the smooth asymptotic, its known regularity range, and the interval conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted series and closed form for g_alpha are legible but formula-sensitive; prose fully supports the resonance-versus-zero dichotomy.

accepted_units.title: Discrepancy as the sharp manifestation of the bias
accepted_units.why_material: Turns the density correction into a supremal interval discrepancy and distinguishes a conjectured asymptotic from unconditional lower and RH-conditional upper information. This is the target sharp statistic to which later smoothing arguments return.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the discrepancy definition, Conjecture 2, and both parts of Theorem 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is fragmented across lines but the normalization, supremum, and theorem directions are recoverable from the text.

accepted_units.title: Exponential-sum cancellation is the central sharpness criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies sums of x^{i gamma} over zeros as the Fourier data controlling interval counts. Under RH, uniform o(T) cancellation on a specified x-range implies both sharp distribution conjectures; the Landau formula also explains why prime-power resonance governs small x and why unconditional control survives only in a narrower range.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Conjecture 3, Theorem 2, and the uniform-Landau-formula discussion needed to interpret both the range and obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several exponents and bounds are formula-sensitive, but the implication and prime-power main-term mechanism are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Short-interval prime fluctuations and zero-sum cancellation constrain each other
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3 gives a two-way, though quantitatively asymmetric, bridge: sufficiently small prime-counting errors in short intervals imply the zero exponential-sum conjecture, while that conjecture forces a weaker short-interval estimate. The normal-fluctuation heuristic supplies scale context without being used as proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Conjecture 4, both directions of Theorem 3, the statistical heuristic, and comparison with a stronger Gonek hypothesis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exponent extraction is somewhat fragile; theorem directions and qualitative strength comparisons are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Strong pair correlation implies the needed exponential cancellation
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the weighted pair-correlation statistic and makes a strengthened, error-sensitive pair-correlation conjecture sufficient for Conjecture 3 and hence sharp fractional-part distribution. The comparison with Montgomery and Chan clarifies that main-term asymptotics alone are not enough for this use.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes F(x,T), Conjecture 5, Theorem 4, and the hierarchy of pair-correlation conjectures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The kernel and x-range are formula-dependent but remain readable in the extraction.

accepted_units.title: Mollification transfers a smooth bias law into a sharp discrepancy lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: Convolves an extremizing interval indicator with a narrow smooth nonnegative kernel, applies the established smooth asymptotic, and uses boundedness of g_alpha plus averaging to recover a nearby interval with the desired discrepancy. This is a reusable smooth-to-sharp lower-bound move.
accepted_units.context_note: The entire short proof is retained so the averaging and epsilon limit are not severed from their setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral formatting is degraded but the convolution, averaging, and limiting argument are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Extremal trigonometric brackets isolate resonance and control the unresolved Fourier tail
accepted_units.why_material: Majorizes and minorizes an interval indicator by optimal degree-J trigonometric polynomials, evaluates low Fourier modes through Landau's formula, isolates exactly the prime-power resonant modes as the g_alpha term, and leaves high modes to Conjecture 3. Choosing the cutoff differently yields the RH bound or the conjectural asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes construction, coefficient bounds, the J0 cutoff, resonant and nonresonant mode analysis, and the final choices of J.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense displayed algebra has extraction risk; the prose and intact inequalities preserve the proof architecture, while exact constants should be checked against the PDF before training.

accepted_units.title: A band-limited interval cutoff converts zero sums into local prime variation
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a Beurling-Selberg-type approximation to an interval with compact Fourier support, controls its endpoint error, then uses Fourier inversion, integration by parts, and the explicit formula to bound the zero exponential sum by the maximum local variation of G(x)=psi(x)-x. This supplies the forward half of the prime-to-zero bridge.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the construction of H and F, their decay and Fourier support, truncation errors, explicit-formula substitution, and the final parameter choice.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy and some symbols are displaced; the sequence of transformations is recoverable, but exact analytic bounds need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Partial summation sends zero-sum cancellation back to short-interval primes
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from the explicit formula for psi(x+y)-psi(x)-y, uses Conjecture 3 and partial summation for medium and large zero ordinates, and bounds small zeros directly. It demonstrates how a spectral cancellation statement becomes an arithmetic local-error estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the high-zero partial summation and the separate low-zero Taylor estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted sums are visually fragmented, but the range split, asymptotic conclusion, and role of partial summation are clear.

accepted_units.title: Pair-correlation second differences control a first-moment zero sum
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a beta-smoothed pair-correlation statistic, bounds the linear exponential sum by its quadratic energy, and rewrites that energy as an exponentially weighted average of D(xe^u,t)-D(x,t). Symmetrization reveals that small multiplicative second differences of normalized pair correlation are the operative regularity signal.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 1, its derivation via G_beta, tail handling, and the choice of beta completing Theorem 4.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed exponents are extraction-sensitive; the normalized statistic, smoothing identity, second-difference structure, and conclusion remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Selberg-class transfer isolates degree and zero-density assumptions
accepted_units.why_material: Specifies the analytic continuation, functional equation, Euler product, coefficient growth, intrinsic degree, zero-counting law, primitivity, RH_F, and a weaker zero-density hypothesis. These are precisely the structural inputs used to generalize the zeta mechanisms without conflating full RH with the weaker hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes all five class conditions and both zero-location hypotheses so later results have self-contained assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The class axioms and prose are clear; a few fractions and conjugation marks should be checked in the PDF for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: General Euler coefficients determine the fractional-part bias for L-functions
accepted_units.why_material: Generalizes Landau's formula with Lambda_F and uses it, together with the zero-density hypothesis, to define g_{F,alpha} and prove the smooth-test-function distribution law. It shows that the same resonance mechanism survives, with its shape now carrying local Euler-factor data.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 2, its nontriviality range, Theorem 5, and the Dirichlet-L corollary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The formula is readable but highly sensitive to displaced exponents and should be verified against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Euler-factor phase predicts translated shortages of Dirichlet zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the generalized density to a Dirichlet character and interprets its complex phase as the location of shortages among fractional parts. The finite-height histograms are framed as an illustration of this analytic prediction rather than evidence establishing the asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the specialized density, shortage locations, empirical statistic definition, sample size, and provenance of the zeros; the plot itself is excluded separately as extraction-defective.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The analytic phase relation is recoverable; assessing visual agreement requires the original figure because the normalized text contains only axes and labels.

accepted_units.title: Sharp distribution and discrepancy bounds extend to primitive Selberg-class functions
accepted_units.why_material: States interval and discrepancy conjectures for F and transfers the smooth-to-sharp lower-bound mechanism. The RH_F upper error explicitly depends on the coefficient-growth exponent, exposing how analytic complexity changes the usable Fourier cutoff.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Conjectures 6-7, the altered cutoff, and both parts of Theorem 6.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem structure is clear; the extracted cutoff numerator is awkward and needs formula verification.

accepted_units.title: General zero sums and generalized prime sums retain the two-way bridge
accepted_units.why_material: Adjusts the zero-sum x-range to the coefficient-growth exponent, gives an explicit formula for the generalized Chebyshev error G_F, and states the two directional implications between short-interval G_F control and exponential-sum cancellation. This distinguishes a structural transfer from a zeta-specific accident.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Conjecture 8, Theorems 7-8, the explicit formula, and Conjecture 9.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several powers are formula-sensitive, but the dependence on theta_F and both implication directions are explicit.

accepted_units.title: The pair-correlation transition zone obstructs higher-degree transfer
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why a naive pair-correlation analog proves the needed zero-sum result for degree one but fails for degree at least two: the transition near x=T^{d_F} lies outside the effective explicit-formula range. The proposed repair is boundedness plus small multiplicative second variation through that zone, which restores the argument.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Murty-Perelli conjecture, the degree-dependent obstruction, Conjecture 11, and Theorem 9.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The scale and qualitative obstruction are clear; the exact normalization and little-o bound in Conjecture 11 should be checked against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From arithmetic resonance to sharp discrepancy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A prime-power resonance first appears as a smooth lower-order density; mollification and extremal Fourier brackets then turn that density into sharp interval discrepancy information while separating resolved resonant modes from an unresolved high-frequency tail.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The full interval asymptotic still depends on uniform zero-sum cancellation, and exact Fourier constants are formula-sensitive in this extraction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One exponential-sum interface links three representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The sums of x^{i gamma} are a common interface: Fourier expansion connects them to fractional-part counts, explicit formulas connect them bidirectionally to local prime fluctuations, and quadratic smoothing connects them to pair correlation and its multiplicative second differences.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The implications are conditional and quantitatively asymmetric; they do not make proof-search failure or a weak bound evidence against the underlying conjectures.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Euler data shifts the bias while analytic degree controls transfer
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across primitive Selberg-class functions, local Euler coefficients determine the shape and phase of the fractional-part bias, while coefficient growth and degree determine the accessible zero-sum range and whether pair-correlation regularity reaches the needed transition zone.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer relies on stated zero-density or RH_F assumptions, the phase illustration is finite-height, and for degree at least two the proposed transition-zone regularity remains conjectural.
